question: On slippery surfaces like snow or ice, which action is recommended before descending steep hills?
options: a:Shift to a low gear to maintain control.,b:Follow closely behind the vehicle in front of you.,c:Pump your brakes continuously to prevent freezing.,d:Use cruise control to keep steady speed.
note: Use a low gear to help maintain traction when going down steep hills; avoid quick stops and follow farther behind other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and exercise caution while crossing or turning at the intersection.

question: Which substances can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, cough syrups, and some over-the-counter cold medicines — all of the above.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only alcoholic beverages.,d:Only prescription medications.
note: Many substances — including depressants, illicit drugs, and certain OTC medicines — impair driving and increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Check side mirrors and look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.,b:Check only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down significantly and merge quickly.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and change lanes.
note: Always check your side mirrors and perform a shoulder check to verify the adjacent lane is clear before changing lanes.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means what?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, traffic beside the broken line may pass when safe, while traffic beside the solid line may not.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Strong emotions impair judgment and attention. Calm down before operating a vehicle so you can focus on driving safely.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which of these should you NOT do?
options: a:Letting go of the steering wheel.,b:Apply your brakes.,c:Press your head firmly against the head restraint.
note: Do not let go of the steering wheel. Brace against the seat and head restraint and be prepared to apply brakes to avoid being pushed into another vehicle.

question: If poor weather reduces visibility, what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Speed up to get off the road quickly.
note: When visibility is reduced, increase following distance to allow more time to react to hazards.

question: How are stopping distances and crash severity affected as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:They increase as a vehicle's speed increases.,b:They decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.,c:They are not affected by a vehicle's speed.
note: As speed increases, both stopping distance and the potential impact severity of a collision increase; maintain greater following distances at higher speeds.

question: Regulatory signs are typically what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Blue,b:Green,c:White
note: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are typically white with black markings and must be obeyed by motorists.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road indicates what?
options: a:A construction zone is ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from either direction.
note: Broken yellow center lines separate two-way traffic and mean passing is allowed when it is safe to do so and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem displayed on the rear of a vehicle indicates what?
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:Slow-moving vehicle.,c:Shoulder work ahead.
note: An orange and red triangle identifies a slow-moving vehicle such as farm equipment or road maintenance vehicles and indicates limited speed.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgment, which is essential for safe driving.,b:If you can walk straight after drinking, you are safe to drive.,c:Being under the legal BAC means your driving isn't impaired.,d:Drinking coffee neutralizes alcohol's effects.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment and decision-making; any amount can degrade driving ability even below legal BAC limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering an interstate from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.,b:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,c:Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and merge when a safe gap appears; do not stop unless necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow warns the signal is changing to red; stop safely if you have not entered the intersection.

question: When involved in a collision, when should you give your name, address, and vehicle registration information to the other drivers?
options: a:Only if the collision caused injury.,b:When property damage totals above $500.,c:Every time you are involved in a collision.
note: You must stop and exchange identification, address, and vehicle registration information with other drivers involved in any crash, regardless of severity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When overtaking another vehicle, how should you pass?
options: a:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,c:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: Pass quickly and safely, then return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: When the gate at a railroad crossing is lowering, how should you react?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait.,b:Speed up and cross the tracks before the gate lowers completely.,c:Drive around the gate.
note: Stop when crossing gates are lowering. Crossing before the gate is fully raised or going around it is unsafe and illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, you must:
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Assume oncoming traffic and pedestrians will yield to you.,c:Never yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians.,d:Only yield if your light is red.
note: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians until it is safe to complete the turn.

question: To check for objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, drivers should do what?
options: a:Only the left outside mirror.,b:Over their left or right shoulder.,c:Only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Look over your left or right shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check blind spots that mirrors do not show.

question: On an interstate, what is a good way to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Change lanes to the left.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down.
note: When safe, move out of the right-hand lane to allow merging traffic space; do not assume merging drivers will yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection. What is the safest action?
options: a:Partially enter the intersection to establish right-of-way.,b:Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely before the light turns red; blocking the intersection may result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed with caution.

question: What is the correct top-to-bottom order of a standard traffic signal?
options: a:Green, red, yellow.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Red, yellow, green.
note: Standard vertical traffic lights from top to bottom are red, then yellow, then green.

question: When a school bus is stopped on the road ahead with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Slow to 10 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Change lanes and drive slowly past the bus.,d:Proceed if no children are visible.
note: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm until it resumes motion and retracts signals.

question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, which action should you NOT take?
options: a:Back up on the road or shoulder.,b:Proceed to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.,c:Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route to your destination.
note: Do not back up on the travel lane or shoulder if you miss an exit. Continue to the next exit and find a safe way to return to your intended route.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: Pull off the traveled lane if possible, turn on hazards, and remain in the vehicle for safety unless immediate danger forces you out.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Oncoming vehicles may appear slower than they are; ensure there is enough space to pass safely before changing lanes.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line permits passing when it is safe; solid lines prohibit passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: Re-enter your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe distance.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).,b:Construction and maintenance warnings.,c:Mileage distances to locations.,d:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.
note: Blue signs are service signs that provide information about motorist services such as rest areas, food, or hospitals.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Use side mirrors and a shoulder check to see vehicles in your blind spot before merging onto the freeway.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Start to prepare to slow down.
note: When a child or pedestrian is about to enter your path, a sharp blast of the horn can warn them and help prevent a collision.

question: What must you do when approaching a pedestrian who uses a guide dog or white cane?
options: a:Honk so they know to clear the way.,b:Swerve quickly around them.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Stop and give the blind pedestrian the right-of-way; do not honk or attempt to steer around them abruptly.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of substance?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant that impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect which abilities?
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can impair judgment, coordination, and the ability to operate a vehicle safely.

question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another driver makes a mistake.,c:When another vehicle is in your way and you want them to move.
note: Only use your horn to warn others of danger or to prevent a collision; do not use it to express frustration or impatience.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Where signs and pavement markings indicate passing is permitted and it is safe.,b:Within an intersection if no oncoming vehicles are present.,c:On a curve if you can see ahead a short distance.,d:Anywhere if you signal before passing.
note: Never pass in intersections or where visibility is blocked by curves or hills; pass only where allowed by markings and when safe.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to you.,b:You must yield to pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to you.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings and must be yielded to; vehicles must stop for pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks when required.

question: What does a green arrow signal require you to do?
options: a:Yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the intersection, then complete the turn.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Ignore any pedestrians in the intersection.,d:Proceed immediately without yielding.
note: A green arrow permits movement in the arrow's direction, but you must first yield to any persons or vehicles still in the intersection.

question: Why is winter driving more hazardous than other seasons?
options: a:There are increased hours of darkness.,b:Road conditions can be affected by freezing temperatures, ice, snow, and fog.,c:Both of the above.
note: Winter brings ice, snow, fog, and longer nights, all of which increase driving risks and require extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general attitude should a driver have about right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Even if you have the legal right-of-way, be prepared to yield if it will help avoid a crash.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.
note: A school crossing (pentagon) warns of children; slow down, watch carefully, and be prepared to stop.

question: If a tire blows out suddenly while you're driving, what steps should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and exit the traffic lane slowly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop quickly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge.,d:Turn on your hazards and speed up to reach the shoulder faster.
note: Grasp the wheel firmly, remove your foot from the gas, lightly apply brakes when safe, and steer gradually off the road once slowed.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three
note: Even one alcoholic drink can impair your driving. It is unsafe to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing can speed up sobering other than time.

question: When ridden on public roadways, bicycles are legally classified as:
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Vehicles.,c:Hazards.,d:Motor vehicles.
note: When bicycles are operated on streets, they are treated as vehicles and bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as motor vehicle drivers.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the lap belt.
note: If your vehicle has lap and shoulder belts, use both for maximum protection. Wearing only one part reduces effectiveness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic; this creates a high risk of collision.

question: Driving noticeably slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may take risky maneuvers to pass you.

question: What qualifies as a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: A distraction is anything that diverts attention from driving and increases the risk of collisions.

question: When following another vehicle at night, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle to avoid blinding the driver ahead.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Neither lane may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite directions of traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you want to change lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes while inside an intersection. Always check mirrors and blind spots before signaling and moving over.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do to re-enter safely?
options: a:Wait until it is safe to do so, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, reduce speed, check traffic, and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe to do so; do not jerk the wheel.

question: Which headlights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beams in rain, snow, sleet, or fog; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drug use?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs worsen reaction time, coordination, alertness, and the ability to concentrate, impairing safe driving.

question: What is the law regarding posters and signs on car windows?
options: a:Are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.,b:Are prohibited by state law if they obstruct a driver's view of the road.,c:Are allowed only if they do not contain offensive language.
note: State law prohibits placing signs or materials on vehicle windows that obstruct the driver's clear view of the roadway.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection tells you to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be cautious, and proceed when safe; it does not require a full stop unless safety demands it.

question: How do you drive defensively?
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
note: Defensive driving requires scanning the road, checking mirrors, and being aware of potential hazards, not just focusing on the vehicle ahead.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety checks should you perform?
options: a:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,b:Buckle your safety belt.,c:Both of the above.
note: Make it a habit to buckle your seat belt and ensure all passengers do the same before starting the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the \Don't Walk\" signal begins flashing and is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?"
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Proceed since you have the green and the pedestrian is mid-street.,d:Honk to make the pedestrian hurry.
note: If a pedestrian is in the intersection when your light turns green, allow them to finish crossing before you proceed.

question: You should avoid using your horn when driving near:
options: a:Drivers whose visibility ahead is limited.,b:Blind pedestrians.,c:Vehicles about to collide with you.,d:Pedestrians in crosswalks at night.
note: Using a horn near a blind pedestrian can be dangerous or disorienting; instead yield and proceed when it is safe.

question: Reaction time is slower after which of the following?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes, reaction time, and judgment, impairing the ability to drive safely even at low levels of consumption.

question: Which factor listed affects how alcohol is absorbed into the body?
options: a:Height,b:Weight,c:Intelligence
note: Alcohol absorption is influenced by body weight, biological sex, food in the stomach, and amount consumed. Only time removes alcohol from the system.

question: Which road surface is most likely to freeze first?
options: a:A tunnel,b:An intersection,c:A bridge
note: Bridges and overpasses cool faster and can freeze before the adjacent roadways.

question: If you are already within an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop.,c:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.
note: If you are committed in the intersection when the light turns yellow, clear it safely rather than stopping abruptly.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Grip the wheel firmly, slow down gradually without heavy braking, and pull off when safe.,b:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,c:Press the brake pedal as hard as possible immediately.,d:Turn sharply toward the nearest shoulder.
note: Keep the vehicle straight, ease off the accelerator, avoid heavy braking, and pull off the road when safe.

question: Approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red traffic signal, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding, like a stop sign.

question: When is highway pavement especially slippery?
options: a:If it has just begun to rain.,b:If it has been raining several hours.,c:If it has been raining for one to two hours.
note: Pavement is often most slippery when rain first begins because oil and dirt on the roadway mix with water, creating a greasy film.

question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, how does traction compare to pavement and what should you do?
options: a:You have less traction than on pavement, so slow down.,b:Your tires grip better than on pavement, so maintain speed.,c:Visibility is always better than on pavement, so speed is fine.,d:Traction is the same as pavement under all conditions.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction; slow down and allow longer stopping distances when driving on gravel or dirt.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on the roadway?
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.,b:Indicate no passing zones.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic traveling in opposite directions; dashed (broken) yellow lines mean passing is permitted when safe.

question: If another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: a:Brake hard to make the pass quicker.,b:Maintain a constant speed and allow the vehicle to pass safely.,c:Speed up to prevent the pass.,d:Move into the passing lane immediately.
note: When being passed, keep a steady speed and allow the other vehicle to complete the pass without increasing your speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it best to change from one lane to another?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Change lanes gradually and carefully, only when necessary and when it is safe to do so, using signals and mirror checks.

question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.,b:Yes, it is always safer than driving faster than other traffic.,c:No, you can block traffic when you drive too slowly.
note: Driving too slowly can impede traffic and may be unsafe; adjust speed to conditions but avoid needlessly blocking traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should position your vehicle:
options: a:Near the centerline.,b:Near the right-hand side of the road.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: When turning left from a two-way street, start in the lane closest to the centerline and turn into the first legal lane on the new street.

question: As you enter a roundabout, who should you yield to?
options: a:Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing, and traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Only to vehicles inside the roundabout.,c:Only to pedestrians but not to vehicles.,d:No one — you have the right-of-way upon entry.
note: Yield to any crossing pedestrians or bicyclists and to vehicles already circulating within the roundabout before entering.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,b:Traffic control devices.,c:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle not visible in mirrors; check over your shoulder before changing lanes to see these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving speed is correct?
options: a:As your speed increases, so should your following distance.,b:As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.,c:Both of the above.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the severity of collisions; you should also increase your following distance as speed rises.

question: Which of these helps reduce road rage?
options: a:Use your horn frequently.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
note: Signaling lane changes courteously and following traffic laws reduces frustration and helps prevent road rage.

question: At a red light that also displays a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,b:You first come to a complete stop.,c:You wait until the light changes.
note: If you are in the lane corresponding to a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction when the way is clear, even if other signals are red.

question: After a train passes and you have stopped at the railroad crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Look for a second train.,b:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.,c:Both of the above.
note: Ensure no other trains are coming and that warning signals have ended before crossing the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in an urban district?
options: a:20 mph.,b:45 mph.,c:30 mph.
note: The statutory speed limit in an urban district is 30 miles per hour unless signs state otherwise.

question: How can you prevent becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax, focus on driving, and plan realistic travel time.,b:Tailgate the car ahead to motivate them.,c:Drive above posted speed limits to avoid delays.,d:Honk frequently to assert your right-of-way.
note: Keep calm, avoid taking others' actions personally, obey speed limits, and allow adequate travel time to reduce aggression.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow arrow means the protected left-turn phase is ending; drivers must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic when the arrow changes from green to yellow.

question: How can you help avoid skids on slippery surfaces?
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
note: Slow before entering a curve because braking on a curve may cause a skid; gradual speed control is safer on slippery surfaces.

question: What does a dashed white line between lanes on a two-lane roadway indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is permitted.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction but passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is permitted.,d:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.
note: White center lines separate traffic moving in the same direction; a dashed line means you may pass when safe.

question: Collisions are more likely to happen under which condition?
options: a:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,b:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.,c:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Crashes are more likely when a vehicle travels at a significantly different speed than surrounding traffic, either faster or slower than the flow.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness and concentration.,b:Reaction time and coordination.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow the nervous system, reducing alertness, reaction time, and coordination.

question: What are "No zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.,b:Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they restrict the truck driver's ability to stop and maneuver safely.
note: No zones are truck blind spots where cars are not visible to the truck driver and where being too close increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.,b:Always maintain your position.,c:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
note: When it is safe to do so, make room for vehicles merging into your lane to help traffic flow and avoid collisions.

question: Distracted driving is defined as what?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving involves anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving and is a major contributing factor to collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Always stop before entering the highway.,b:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
note: Search for a safe gap in traffic and merge smoothly; do not stop on the ramp unless no safe gap exists.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Whenever you need to use them.,c:Before you get into the car.
note: Adjust mirrors, your seat, and fasten your safety belt before you begin driving to ensure clear visibility and control.

question: When driving in fog, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.
note: Use low beams and reduce speed in fog; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility. If visibility is severely limited, pull off the road safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what conditions should the posted maximum speed limit be driven?
options: a:Only under ideal conditions.,b:During the day.,c:During the night.
note: The maximum posted speed is for ideal driving conditions; reduce speed for weather, visibility, and traffic conditions.

question: Where is a road most likely to be icy after precipitation on a cold day?
options: a:In shaded areas.,b:On a hilly open road.,c:In a residential road with many houses.,d:On bridges only.
note: Shaded parts of the roadway freeze first and thaw last, making them more likely to remain icy.

question: Which headlights should be used to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Low beams should be used in fog, rain, and snow because high beams reflect and worsen visibility.

question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution; slow down and be prepared to yield or stop if necessary.

question: When driving in fog, what is the correct combination of speed and lights?
options: a:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,b:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.,c:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
note: Slow down and use low beams in fog; high beams reduce visibility by reflecting light back.

question: When weather or lighting conditions require headlights, which should you use?
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Use your fog lights.,c:Use your parking lights.,d:Use your high beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams can reflect back and cause glare, reducing visibility.

question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
note: When parked on a slope, turn the wheels so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

question: A stopped school bus is ahead of you with its red lights flashing. How should you respond?
options: a:Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.,b:Stop and proceed when you think all of the children have exited the bus.,c:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights, all approaching drivers must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing. On divided highways, the rule may differ for drivers on the opposite side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, you arrive at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; in this case you are to the right of the vehicle on your left.

question: If you become tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window.,c:Drink coffee.
note: Stopping to rest or switching drivers is the safest way to handle drowsiness; short fixes like coffee are unreliable.

question: What does a dashed yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; a dashed yellow line means passing is allowed when it is safe.

question: When must you stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:When you are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.,b:When there isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,c:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.
note: Expect trains on any track at any time. Only enter the tracks if you can fully clear them; never stop on the tracks.

question: Which statement about using your feet while driving is correct?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.,c:You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake to maintain smooth control and avoid accidental inputs.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on the driving task.
note: Driving over the speed limit, too slowly for conditions, or too fast for the circumstances are common contributing factors to crashes.

question: If the center of the roadway is marked with one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You are allowed to pass other vehicles on the left if the way is clear.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You may only make right turns from this lane.,d:Passing is allowed only during daylight hours.
note: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your original lane?
options: a:Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,b:See the vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:Have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.
note: Only move back into your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe distance.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:Directly behind the body.,b:On the immediate left of the cab.,c:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots on both sides and directly behind; if you cannot see the driver's face in the mirror, they likely cannot see you.

question: If you are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection until it passes.,c:Pull to the left of the intersection and stop.,d:Speed up and clear the intersection quickly.
note: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in an intersection, finish crossing, then pull to the right and stop to yield the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals for you to stop while the light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Obey the officer.
note: Instructions from a police officer take precedence over traffic signals or signs; you must follow the officer's directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is correct regarding checking for blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over the appropriate shoulder (right for right lane change, left for left).,b:Turn and look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.,c:If you have two outside mirrors you have no blind spots.,d:Only signal; mirrors are sufficient to change lanes.
note: Signal, check mirrors, and look over the left or right shoulder as needed to ensure the adjacent lane is clear of vehicles or bicycles.

question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?
options: a:Drive only in the center of the roadway.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
note: Never drive into floodwaters; even shallow water can hide hazards and can sweep a vehicle away.

question: If you've had several beers, how are the effects of alcohol reduced?
options: a:Only by waiting several hours for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,b:By taking a cold shower to revive you.,c:By drinking coffee to sober up.,d:By exercising vigorously to speed elimination.
note: Only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol; coffee, showers, or exercise do not speed this process.

question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,b:Keep your wheels facing straight.,c:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
note: When parked uphill without a curb, turn the front wheels to the right (toward the edge) so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
options: a:Brake as hard as possible immediately.,b:Turn off the ignition to stop wheel power.,c:Ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.,d:Steer opposite the skid and pump the brakes.
note: When skidding, release the accelerator or brake and steer into the skid (in the same direction the rear is sliding) to help regain control.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.,b:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,c:Increase as vehicle speed increases.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and make collisions more severe due to greater energy involved.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.,b:Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions to keep tire contact with the road and lower the chance of hydroplaning.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates which passing rule?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow line on your side means you may cross the centerline to pass when it is safe to do so.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,b:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,c:Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.
note: Always be prepared to yield and take whatever action is necessary to avoid striking a pedestrian, regardless of their compliance with laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure for making a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow down, and approach the turn from the lane nearest the right curb before turning.,b:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.,c:Approach from the left lane and move toward the middle before turning.,d:Turn without signaling if no traffic is visible.
note: Before turning right, signal, slow, and use the lane nearest the right curb, staying close to the curb or edge of the road.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Turn on low beam headlights as daylight fades to make your vehicle more visible; use high beams only when no other vehicles are present.

question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do?
options: a:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.,b:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,c:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.
note: Always reduce speed before entering a curve; braking in a curve can cause a skid and you may not see hazards ahead.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance; look well ahead to allow time and space to react safely to hazards.

question: When passing a line of parked cars, what should you expect?
options: a:Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.,b:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.,c:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
note: People or vehicles can emerge from between parked cars; maintain a safe space and be ready to react.

question: What is the primary purpose of rumble strips on the roadway?
options: a:To alert inattentive drivers via vibration and sound that their vehicle is leaving the travel lane.,b:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:To warn drivers of potential tire problems.,d:To slow traffic with noise only.
note: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn drivers they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or curve.

question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It notifies other road users of your intentions.,b:It is illegal to turn off a signal before completing a turn.,c:It is always unsafe to turn off your signal early.,d:Signals increase your turn speed.
note: Continuous signaling during turns, lane changes, or stops lets drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection where all four corners have stop signs, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you.,b:The driver on your left.,c:The driver across from your vehicle.,d:The driver who signals first.
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive; if multiple arrive simultaneously, yield to the right.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you ensure regarding lanes?
options: a:You must have your vehicle fully in the left lane before and during the pass.,b:Stay in the same lane and squeeze by the motorcycle.,c:Pass with as little space as possible to reduce time alongside them.,d:Pass only when the motorcycle moves onto the shoulder.
note: When passing, you must fully occupy the left lane (not share it with the motorcycle) and leave a full lane of space.

question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:
options: a:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Yield to entering traffic.,c:Drive in a clockwise direction.
note: Enter a roundabout only after yielding to traffic already in the circle; roundabouts flow counterclockwise around a central island.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
note: Leave a note securely attached with your name, phone number, and address, and report the incident if required.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They are smaller, harder to see, and have less developed reflexes than adults.,b:They always follow traffic rules precisely.,c:They require more space because of bicycle size.,d:They can signal better than adults.
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see; give them more space, especially near schools and playgrounds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where drivers arrive at the same time, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: When vehicles arrive simultaneously without signals, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: What do temporary signs in construction and maintenance work areas look like?
options: a:Have a red background with green writing.,b:Have an orange background with black writing.,c:Have a yellow background with blue writing.
note: Work zone signs use an orange background with black lettering or symbols to warn drivers of temporary hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, what should you do to check for oncoming traffic or pedestrians?
options: a:Look to the sides of your vehicle to check what is coming.,b:Stop, listen, and then proceed without looking.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that appear stopped for no reason.,d:Only look straight ahead before proceeding.
note: When approaching places where others may cross your path, look to the left and right sides of your vehicle to be sure nothing is coming.

question: Before entering an intersection, in what order should you look?
options: a:Left, your right, then your left again.,b:Right.,c:Left.
note: Look left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection because vehicles from the left will be closer and may pose an immediate hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:If you entered the intersection on the green light.,b:During rush hour traffic.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it; blocking an intersection is prohibited.

question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: Return to your lane only when you can clearly see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, and always check blind spots before moving over.

question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line signify?
options: a:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.
note: Only traffic adjacent to the dashed line may cross the center to pass; the side with the solid line may not pass.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from lights limit how far ahead you can see at night; use headlights and extra caution.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Challenge them.
note: Avoid competing with aggressive drivers. Safest option is to yield space and let them pass or go ahead.

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination faster.,c:Turn up the radio volume to stay awake.,d:Open all windows and keep driving.
note: Signs of fatigue (heavy eyelids, lane drifting) mean you should stop and rest or switch drivers to avoid a crash.

question: The only effective method to remove alcohol from your body is to:
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait; allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,c:Take a cold shower.,d:Exercise vigorously to speed up elimination.
note: Alcohol is removed from the body only by time; nothing you eat, drink, or do will speed up the metabolism of alcohol.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended and red lights flashing, what must drivers do?
options: a:Continue driving when you think most kids are done exiting the bus.,b:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,c:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.
note: If a school bus is stopped with the stop arm extended and red lights flashing, drivers must stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted and the lights turn off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto a one-way street, from which lane should you start the turn?
options: a:Any lane (as long as it is safe).,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:The lane in the center of the road.
note: When turning left from a one-way onto another one-way street, begin the turn from the far left lane unless otherwise directed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing, what should you verify?
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:You have sounded your horn to warn the other driver.,c:You have flashed your headlights.,d:The vehicle you passed has changed speed.
note: Only return to your lane when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to drive off the paved roadway onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You may not drive off the paved roadway or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle under any circumstances.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:If you are stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.,b:Only if you are involved in a collision.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.,d:Only during a vehicle inspection.
note: You must carry proof of financial responsibility and present it to an officer upon request after a traffic stop or collision.

question: Roads are especially slippery just after it begins to rain. What should you do?
options: a:Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.,b:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.,c:Test your tires' traction while going uphill.
note: Wet roads reduce tire traction; drive more slowly and avoid fast turns or sudden stops until the road surface improves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing, when should you move back into the right lane?
options: a:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Move back into the lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: If you are worried, nervous, or angry, what should you do about driving?
options: a:Are more in touch with their senses and will be more precise drivers.,b:Should let someone else drive.,c:Will drive no differently than they would if thinking clearly.
note: Emotional distress can impair driving ability; if you are upset or distracted, have someone else drive whenever possible.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, how should you react?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.,c:Tap or pump the brakes.
note: If a tire blows out, release the accelerator and slow down gradually; avoid heavy braking until the vehicle has slowed considerably.

question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a driver 21 or older considered to be driving under the influence in Alabama?
options: a:0.04 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: A BAC of 0.08% or higher is the standard limit for drivers 21 and older for DUI enforcement.

question: When driving on snow or ice, how should you make speed and direction changes?
options: a:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.,b:It is safe to use your cruise control.,c:Drive as you would under normal conditions.
note: On snow or ice, make gradual steering and speed adjustments; never use cruise control because it can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is correct?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never an unsafe practice.,c:Your driving speed doesn't affect safety.,d:Driving below the speed limit always improves safety.
note: Driving substantially below the flow of traffic can create hazards as other drivers make risky passes; match traffic speed when safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you obey instructions from school crossing guards?
options: a:At all times when they are directing pedestrians and traffic.,b:Only during posted school hours.,c:Only if children are visible nearby.,d:Only when accompanied by a police officer.
note: Drivers must always obey directions from school crossing guards whenever they are on duty.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Steer a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
note: When passing between oncoming and parked vehicles, aim for a midpoint to allow clearance on both sides and reduce collision risk.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are small and hard to see, what should drivers do?
options: a:Slow down when driving.,b:Make constant visual checks.,c:Share a lane with a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are easily missed in blind spots or quick glances; drivers should constantly check for them and avoid sharing a lane.

question: What is the definition of a crosswalk?
options: a:Another name for a four-way intersection.,b:An area designated for road construction workers.,c:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
note: Crosswalks mark where pedestrians are likely to cross and may be marked or unmarked; drivers must yield as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic control signal is not operating, what should you do at the intersection?
options: a:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way as you would at an all-way stop.,b:Proceed if the intersection appears clear without stopping.,c:Drive quickly through to avoid blocking traffic.,d:Follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.
note: When signals are out, treat the intersection as an all-way stop: stop, then yield in order of arrival.

question: In a vehicle equipped with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride?
options: a:The front seat.,b:The back seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Airbags can be dangerous to children; people aged 12 and under should ride in the back seat for maximum safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but traffic ahead is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.,c:Turn left and find another route.
note: Do not enter an intersection you cannot clear. If traffic is blocked ahead, remain behind the stop line until the way is clear.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,b:Require the pedestrian to yield to you.,c:Honk to make them aware of your presence.,d:Drive slowly past without stopping.
note: Pedestrians who are blind or partially sighted using a cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive more slowly than the flow of traffic, what is the most likely outcome?
options: a:You will interfere with traffic and could be cited.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will demonstrate defensive driving.,d:You will reduce the risk of collisions significantly.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow can block traffic and may result in a citation; match the flow when safe and legal.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.,b:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,c:It is an activity that draws the attention of other drivers.
note: Cell phone use while driving takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving tasks, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: You are approaching an intersection at speed when the light turns yellow. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up to cross before the light turns red.,b:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,c:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed through cautiously.

question: If the rear of your car begins skidding to the left, what should you do?
options: a:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,b:Steer to the left.,c:Steer to the right.
note: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go (into the skid) to regain control.

question: If a driver is tailgating you on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Apply your brakes suddenly to warn them.,c:Reduce your speed gradually to encourage them to pass or change lanes.,d:Maintain speed and refuse to yield.
note: If someone is following too closely, slow down gradually or, if possible, change lanes so the tailgater can pass safely.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Farther behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.,b:To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.,c:Closer behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.
note: Trucks have larger blind spots and take longer to stop, so maintain more distance when following them than you would a passenger vehicle.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to scare them away.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane.
note: Animals may bolt into the road unpredictably; slow down and proceed cautiously, anticipating additional animals.

question: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, what should a driver do?
options: a:Have their exhaust system checked regularly to be sure there are no leaks.,b:Keep their engine turned off when their vehicle is enclosed in a garage.,c:Both of the above.
note: Carbon monoxide is odorless and deadly; regularly inspect the exhaust system and never run a vehicle in an enclosed space.

question: A driver's license is considered a:
options: a:Right.,b:Requirement.,c:Privilege.,d:Guarantee of safe driving.
note: A driver's license is a privilege granted by the state and may be suspended or revoked for violations.

question: When a large truck turns right onto a multi-lane street, what might it need to do?
options: a:Swing wide to complete the right turn.,b:Always stay in the right-most lane during the turn.,c:Complete the turn in either lane as it chooses.,d:Cut directly across lanes without signaling.
note: Because the rear wheels track a shorter path, long vehicles often need to swing wide when making right turns.

question: On interstate highways, drivers are required to:
options: a:Use cruise control at all times.,b:Be constantly alert.,c:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,d:Both of the above.
note: Driving on interstates requires both the ability to safely operate at higher speeds and constant alertness to traffic and hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,b:Change lanes without signaling.,c:If you miss your exit, you must go to the next exit.
note: Safe interstate practice includes signaling every lane change. Changing lanes without signaling is unsafe and not permitted.

question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?
options: a:Merge into a different lane when possible.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down.
note: If it is safe, change lanes to create a gap for entering vehicles; if not possible, adjust your speed to help them merge.

question: When following a motorcycle, why should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle?
options: a:Passenger vehicle.,b:Motorcycle.,c:Station wagon.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and are less visible; leave extra space to react if they brake or fall.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?
options: a:Attempt to change lanes within an intersection.,b:Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes while inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, always check mirrors and look over your shoulder to check the blind spot.

question: Which action tends to block the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of driving.,d:Driving at posted speeds.
note: Rubbernecking slows traffic and contributes to congestion; keep moving unless emergency requires you to stop.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill on a hill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight.,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,c:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
note: When parking downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or edge so the vehicle will roll away from traffic into the curb or edge.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:Expect the unexpected — children can be unpredictable.,b:Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.,c:Beep your horn to alert them.,d:Assume they will always obey traffic rules.
note: Children on bicycles are unpredictable; watch for sudden changes in direction and give them extra space.

question: In rainy weather, when is the roadway most slippery?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:If it has been raining all day.
note: Road surfaces are often most slippery just after the rain begins because oil and dirt on the pavement mix with the water creating a greasy film.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, who must you yield to?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians — you must yield to them.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.,c:You never have to yield when turning left.,d:Only to bicyclists.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians crossing the intersection.

question: What is the term for slowing down just to look at a crash or unusual sight and what does it do?
options: a:Rubbernecking — it causes traffic congestion.,b:Defensive driving — it prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Careful observation — it improves traffic flow.,d:Sightseeing — it helps emergency responders.
note: Rubbernecking (slowing to look) contributes to congestion and should be avoided unless necessary.

question: As the percentage of alcohol (BAC) in your blood increases, you become:
options: a:More intoxicated.,b:More coordinated.,c:More sober.
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measures alcohol in the bloodstream; higher BAC levels cause greater impairment of judgment and motor skills.

question: Large trucks are most likely to lose speed when they are:
options: a:Driving down long, gradual hills.,b:Driving in long, gradual curves.,c:Driving up long or steep hills.,d:Making quick lane changes.
note: Because of their weight, large trucks often lose speed when climbing long or steep hills and need extra space to accelerate.

question: If you are under 21, driving with what blood alcohol level can lead to license suspension?
options: a:0.08 percent or more.,b:0.15 percent or more.,c:Any amount.
note: Alabama enforces a zero-tolerance policy for under-21 drivers; any detectable alcohol can result in license suspension.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean for drivers turning in that direction?
options: a:You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.,b:You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,c:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the green arrow's protection is ending; if you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,c:Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing red light means stop (like a stop sign); yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: Which behavior may identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Having many passengers in the vehicle.,c:Driving unusually slowly.,d:Keeping a consistent, legal speed.
note: Aggressive drivers often perform erratic lane changes and other unsafe maneuvers; avoid challenging them and get out of their way.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, what is the correct action?
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road.,b:Look straight ahead.,c:Look toward the center of the roadway.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim bright lights, look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded and to keep enough view of the roadway to stay on course.

question: Prior to entering a curve, what is the correct action?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control and avoid braking sharply while turning, which can cause skids.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Often, to observe how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:Only when changing lanes.,d:Every 10 minutes.
note: Frequently checking your mirrors helps you know the positions of nearby vehicles and avoid surprises.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating you have enough space.

question: What does a \No passing zone\" sign indicate?"
options: a:That it is not safe to pass.,b:To speed up slightly.,c:To maintain a steady speed.
note: A No Passing Zone sign marks an area where passing is illegal because conditions make it unsafe to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane should you use?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street, begin from the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the first legal lane in that direction.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Pull over quickly.,c:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
note: Keep a firm grip, maintain direction, ease off the gas, and brake gently; then pull off safely when you can.

question: What should you do when taking any medicine with regard to driving?
options: a:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,b:Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.,c:Have someone follow you home.
note: Consult your doctor or pharmacist about how medications might affect your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an octagonal sign, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Slow down but proceed if clear.,c:Turn right if possible.,d:Yield only to the vehicle on your right.
note: An octagonal eight-sided sign always means \Stop\" — come to a full stop and yield as necessary before proceeding."

question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drug effects from your body?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Give your body time.,c:Breathe in some fresh air.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and remove its impairing effects.

question: In very foggy conditions you should slow down and use which lights?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers.,b:Turn your lights to their high beam setting.,c:Turn your lights to their low beam setting.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility. Use fog lights if equipped, in addition to low beams.

question: If you must park where parking is not usual, what should you ensure?
options: a:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,b:Park with your reverse lights on.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: Drivers must make sure parked vehicles do not create hazards; wherever you park, ensure your vehicle is visible to approaching drivers.

question: Holding a driver license is considered what?
options: a:Requirement.,b:Privilege, not a right.,c:Right, not a privilege.
note: A driver's license is a privilege earned and maintained under the law, not an absolute right.

question: When is it lawful to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When the warning lights are not flashing.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:Never.
note: Never go around or under a lowered gate. Wait until the gate is fully raised and signals have stopped.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:Blind spots are eliminated if the vehicle has an outside mirror on each side.,c:Blind spots can be checked using the rearview mirror alone.,d:Blind spots only exist at low speeds.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to which of the following?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,b:Passing cars only.,c:No one; left-turning vehicles always have priority.,d:Only to vehicles with flashing lights.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and any pedestrians or bicyclists crossing the intersection.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Stay in your lane and slow down but do not stop.,c:Drive quickly to the nearest intersection and stop there.,d:Pull into the left lane to let it pass.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until the vehicle has passed.

question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When the driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,c:When you signal your intention for three seconds.
note: Return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so; always check blind spots.

question: When exiting the interstate, when should you begin reducing your speed?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then slow to the exit ramp's posted advisory speed.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Four-way hazard flashers.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Low beams reduce glare from reflections in fog, rain, or snow and improve visibility.

question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving?
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.
note: Constantly observe the road ahead, to the sides, and behind to detect threats early and adjust speed or position as needed.
