question: Excessive speed increases the likelihood of what outcome?
options: a:Serious bodily injury and death.,b:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,c:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.
note: Speeding increases crash risk and severity and does not reliably reduce overall travel time.

question: When you drive through a construction zone, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Stop to watch the workers.,b:Decrease your following distance.,c:Pass the construction zone carefully and not 'rubberneck.'
note: Avoid slowing down just to look at events in a work zone (rubbernecking); drive through carefully to avoid congestion and hazards.

question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors, what should you do?
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Always slow down in your lane.,d:Assume other drivers will yield to you.
note: Check mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to ensure the blind spot is clear.

question: Is it ever allowed to drive while under the influence of medications that impair your driving?
options: a:No — driving while impaired by medication is not allowed.,b:Only if a doctor prescribed them.,c:Only if you do not feel drowsy.,d:Yes, if they are over-the-counter medications.
note: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance—prescription, over-the-counter, or illicit—that impairs your ability to drive safely.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Vision.,b:Balance.,c:Judgment.
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, which then leads to other skill deterioration.

question: What are construction zone signs typically like in shape and color?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with an orange background and black symbols.,b:Round signs with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square signs with white and red coloring.,d:Rectangular green signs with white letters.
note: Work zone signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols and are often diamond-shaped or rectangular.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.,c:Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.
note: If hydroplaning occurs, ease off the accelerator and slow gradually without heavy braking; sudden inputs can worsen loss of control.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what braking action should you take?
options: a:Brake abruptly.,b:Brake lightly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: Do not use the brakes during a skid; focus on steering to regain control and stabilize the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.,b:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.,c:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
note: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check for vehicles to the side and behind, then watch the vehicle ahead in the gap you intend to use.

question: How can you reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Make abrupt turns to test traction.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.,d:Drive at the posted speed regardless of conditions.
note: To avoid hydroplaning, reduce speed on wet roads and maintain tires so they channel water away effectively.

question: As a driver, what areas around your vehicle should you monitor?
options: a:Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of your vehicle.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Stare directly in front of the car at all times.,d:Only check the mirrors once per mile.
note: Good drivers are aware of what is happening beside, ahead, and behind their vehicle to anticipate hazards.

question: When a school bus is stopped on your side of the road with red lights flashing, what is required?
options: a:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,b:Slow down to a maximum of 10 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Change lanes and pass slowly.,d:Proceed if you are on a different street.
note: You must stop for a school bus with red flashing lights on your side of the road until the signals are turned off and the stop arm is retracted.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,c:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots and block your view; increasing distance lets you see more of the road ahead and keeps you out of the vehicle's blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,b:You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.,c:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.
note: Follow directions at railroad crossings: if a flagger, sign, or warning signal directs you to stop, you must do so.

question: How can drowsiness affect your driving?
options: a:Make you feel better.,b:Help you to be a better driver.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Drowsiness slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment similar to alcohol or drugs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.,b:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,c:All approaching vehicles.
note: When turning left you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and others with the right-of-way.

question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?
options: a:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,b:Stay within that speed range.,c:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.
note: Adjust your speed to travel smoothly with the flow of traffic within posted limits; vehicles traveling at similar speeds reduce crash risk.

question: How can you keep aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.
note: Regularly check your rearview mirror to monitor vehicles behind you and help anticipate traffic changes.

question: Before driving, from which vehicle surfaces should you remove snow, frost, and ice?
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:Just the windshield and passenger window.,c:All windows.
note: Clear all windows and mirrors so you have full visibility before driving.

question: If you observe heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, you should:
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.,b:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue driving.,d:Continue at normal speed but use your horn to warn others.
note: If the road ahead is obscured by heavy smoke, slow down immediately, move to the right, and stop off the roadway until it is safe to proceed.

question: When must vehicles stopped behind a school bus remain stopped?
options: a:The stop arm is retracted.,b:All students are off the bus.,c:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: Remain stopped until the bus's red lights are off, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus begins moving again.

question: If you have a sudden tire blowout while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Use the brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the wheel firmly, gradually slow by easing off the gas and braking lightly, and steer to a safe stop.

question: Tailgating (driving too closely to another vehicle's bumper) can do what?
options: a:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,b:Cannot result in a traffic citation.,c:Reduces collisions by preventing being 'cut off.'
note: Tailgating can provoke aggressive responses, increase crash risk, and may result in legal consequences; it should be avoided.

question: When an oncoming car has very bright headlights at night, how should you react?
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look below their headlights.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights; look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle has passed.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing for traffic in either direction.

question: What does a steady green traffic signal allow approaching drivers to do?
options: a:Increase their speed to quickly clear the intersection.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Continue through the intersection or make permitted turns when the way is clear.
note: A steady green signal allows drivers to proceed straight or turn where permitted, but they must yield to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.

question: What is the crash risk effect of a BAC of 0.02 percent?
options: a:Won't put other drivers at risk.,b:Will double your chances of having an accident.,c:Won't have any effect on your driving.
note: Even low BAC levels (0.02%) significantly increase crash risk compared to sober driving.

question: To whom must you give the right-of-way?
options: a:In a marked crosswalk.,b:In any crosswalk or intersection.,c:Crossing any street.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in marked or unmarked crosswalks and should generally yield to anyone crossing the street for safety.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,b:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,c:At all times.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and stop for them when necessary; yield to anyone already in the intersection or crosswalk.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
note: Legal prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving; it's illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,b:Often, even at controlled intersections.,c:Never; it confuses other drivers.
note: Never assume others will yield. Give up your right-of-way whenever doing so prevents a crash.

question: Traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance areas are normally what color?
options: a:Red.,b:Orange.,c:Yellow.
note: Orange warning signs, cones, and barriers are used in work zones to alert drivers to construction and maintenance activities.

question: If a road is slippery, how should your following distance change?
options: a:No different than normal.,b:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,c:Closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: On slippery roads you need more distance to stop, so increase your following distance beyond the normal safe gap.

question: When driving in fog what lighting and speed practices are recommended?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: Reduce speed and use low beams in fog; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road safely and wait.

question: What does a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line mean regarding passing?
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Not permitted from either direction.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: Passing is allowed for the lane next to the broken yellow line and prohibited for the lane next to the solid line.

question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for traffic in your blind spot?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the left side mirror.
note: Look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

question: What can happen if a driver leaves a gas station without paying for gas?
options: a:Have their license suspended.,b:Be given a warning.,c:Not face any consequences.
note: Driving off without paying for fuel is a Class A misdemeanor in Alabama; after conviction, a driver's license may be suspended.

question: To be able to turn quickly and safely, where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel for better control and quicker, safer steering responses.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what is the safest action?
options: a:Switch your lights to high beams.,b:Turn your lights on and off.,c:Look toward the right edge of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being temporarily blinded and keep your vehicle in your lane.

question: What do yellow lines on the roadway separate?
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.,d:Bicycle lanes from vehicle lanes.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads and separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Leave the front wheels straight.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away so the vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you through a red light, what should you do?
options: a:Follow the officer's directions and go through the intersection.,b:Stop until the light turns green.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,d:Ignore the officer and obey the light.
note: Instructions from police directing traffic override posted signals and must be followed.

question: When entering the interstate, after finding a gap and signaling, what should you do?
options: a:Merge carefully into the gap.,b:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have the right-of-way.,c:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.
note: Identify a gap, accelerate to match traffic speed, signal, and merge smoothly and carefully when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on the interstate?
options: a:70 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:80 mph.
note: The statutory speed limit on interstates in Alabama is 70 miles per hour unless signs indicate a different limit.

question: When backing up your vehicle, what is the proper way to look?
options: a:Look through the rear window.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Press hard on the gas pedal.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window; mirrors do not show directly behind the vehicle and at low speeds you should back up slowly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curbside parking spot, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a large enough gap so you can accelerate to the speed of traffic.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.,d:Honk before entering to warn other drivers.
note: Merge only when there's a gap that allows you to reach the speed of surrounding traffic safely.

question: When a pedestrian guided by a dog or with a white cane is crossing, what must drivers do?
options: a:Always yield the right-of-way to that pedestrian.,b:Only yield if you are at a marked crosswalk.,c:Tell them where it is safe to cross.,d:Proceed if they are not in your lane.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane regardless of crosswalk markings.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what should you do to alert others?
options: a:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road as soon as it's safe.,b:Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.,c:Signal and move into the slow lane and continue driving.,d:Turn off your lights to conserve battery.
note: If your vehicle breaks down, get it off the road if possible and use emergency flashers to make it visible to other drivers.

question: If you intend to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid?
options: a:Assuming the other driver will make space for you to return to the lane.,b:Assuming the other driver will maintain a constant speed.,c:Assuming signaling guarantees a safe pass.,d:Assuming the road ahead is clear.
note: Do not assume other drivers will yield space for you; ensure the lane is clear and you can safely return before passing.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street, how should you respond?
options: a:Do not have to stop for them.,b:Must stop for them.,c:Should honk your horn at them.
note: Even if pedestrians are crossing unlawfully, drivers must yield and take actions to avoid striking them.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:At all times — they always have the right-of-way.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.,c:Only when a crossing guard is present.,d:Only at marked crosswalks.
note: Pedestrians using white canes or guide dogs must be yielded to at all times, regardless of crosswalk markings.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the edge of the pavement, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.,c:Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.
note: Hold steady, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gently. Wait until speed is reduced and traffic is clear before returning to the road.

question: What should you check before bringing your vehicle to a stop at a traffic signal or sign?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Press down hard on the accelerator.,c:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
note: Check your mirrors to be aware of traffic behind and around you before braking to stop smoothly.

question: If you are involved in a collision, how should you treat injured people?
options: a:Avoid moving the injured unless absolutely necessary.,b:Move the injured to their desired location.,c:Insist the injured are fine without immediate medical attention.
note: Do not move injured persons unless they are in immediate danger (fire, etc.). Keep them comfortable and wait for emergency medical help.

question: How should you drive on a dimly lit street at night?
options: a:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.,b:Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.
note: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within your headlight range and adjust for poor visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the statutory speed limit on a country paved road?
options: a:45 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:30 mph.,d:55 mph.
note: On country paved roads the default (statutory) speed limit is 45 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: If you plan to pass a pedestrian while an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.,b:Keep your speed steady because the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,c:Honk to make the pedestrian move over.,d:Quickly swerve into the shoulder to pass.
note: If possible, handle one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian only if it is safe.

question: When is it necessary to use your low beam headlights?
options: a:On a freeway.,b:In fog.,c:On a lighted street.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow because high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: You are approaching a steady yellow traffic signal and have not entered the intersection. What should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal is about to change to red. If you have not entered the intersection, slow and stop safely.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle approaching with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.
note: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes, positioning parallel to the curb.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what may they do legally?
options: a:They may use the left lane.,b:They may cut through all lanes at once.,c:They must dismount and walk their bike.,d:They must always stay to the right.
note: Bicyclists may use the left lane when making a left turn, so expect to see them there.

question: How far should you follow a large truck on the freeway compared to a passenger vehicle?
options: a:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.,b:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.,c:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.
note: Leave extra space behind trucks so you can see around them and have more time to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful?
options: a:Passing another vehicle in a marked no-passing zone.,b:Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,c:Both of the above.,d:Passing on a two-lane road when the vehicle ahead signals a left turn.
note: It is illegal to pass in marked no-passing zones and to pass another vehicle while going over a railroad crossing; both actions are prohibited.

question: To help prevent eye fatigue when driving at night, you should:
options: a:Continue moving your eyes and scanning the road.,b:Stare straight ahead.,c:Rest your eyes by closing them for a couple of seconds at a time.
note: Reduce eye fatigue at night by scanning from center to sides and near to far, keeping your eyes active rather than fixed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you come to an intersection and your view to the side is blocked, what should you do?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Slow down and look both ways.,c:Maintain your speed and look both ways.
note: When visibility is obstructed, stop and slowly inch forward until you have a clear view of cross traffic before proceeding.

question: Which statement about driving while taking medications is correct?
options: a:Medications are safe to take at any time, if prescribed by a doctor.,b:Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.,c:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving; many cold medicines cause drowsiness.

question: Which best describes how a defensive driver thinks?
options: a:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,b:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate possible errors by others and are prepared to compensate to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle under which circumstances?
options: a:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop, and where a red traffic light is displayed.,b:Only where there is a red traffic light.,c:Only if a police officer orders it and no lights are present.,d:Only at marked stop signs.
note: You must stop when directed by a police officer and at steady or flashing red signals; always obey officer instructions.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles can stop more quickly, and following too closely reduces your ability to avoid a collision if they brake suddenly.

question: Which statement about blind spots is accurate?
options: a:Large trucks have larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:Blind spots are eliminated by one outside mirror.,c:Blind spots can be checked using only the rearview mirror.,d:Blind spots disappear at highway speeds.
note: Even with rearview and outside mirrors, blind spots exist; large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

question: What is a potential effect of taking a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can interact with alcohol to impair driving ability and reaction time.

question: When driving through a construction zone, what should you expect?
options: a:Slightly increase your speed.,b:Expect the unexpected.,c:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones present changing conditions and hazards; reduce speed and drive with extra caution for workers and equipment.

question: If you want to enter the freeway but there is no gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.,b:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.
note: Slow on the ramp to wait for a safe gap; do not stop at the end of the ramp where you cannot accelerate to merge safely.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,b:Allowed from both directions.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mark opposite-direction traffic and prohibit passing for both directions.

question: When you encounter orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what is required?
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and reduce your speed.,b:Change lanes immediately and maintain your speed.,c:Ignore the signs if traffic is light.,d:Speed up to clear the zone quickly.
note: Work zones can have workers, slow equipment, and lane closures; slow down and be prepared to stop.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to the curb, but not away from it.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: Signal both when pulling next to a curb and when pulling away to inform other road users of your intended movement.

question: At a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Be alert for vehicles that must stop at all crossings and for multiple trains.,b:Proceed quickly if you don't see a train.,c:Only watch for trains in one direction.,d:Ignore stopped vehicles in the area.
note: Approach crossings with caution, watch for vehicles that must stop (school buses, hazmat trucks), and for trains from either direction.

question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?
options: a:Are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:Are being tailgated by another driver.,c:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If you are being tailgated, leave extra room in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking; slow gradually or change lanes if safe.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is allowed?
options: a:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,b:You must stay within your lane.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and indicate lane changes or passing are permitted when safe.

question: You want to turn right but see a pedestrian with a guide dog at the corner ready to cross. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the person crosses the street.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,c:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or canes have the right-of-way; wait for them to complete crossing before turning.

question: What must approaching drivers do when they see a red traffic signal?
options: a:Continue driving through the intersection without stopping.,b:Increase their speed to quickly clear the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop.
note: Drivers must stop at a steady red light and remain stopped until the signal changes to green or a lawful turn on red is permitted.

question: If you see pedestrians near the road, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass with caution.,b:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: If pedestrians are near the roadway, reduce speed and be prepared to stop if someone steps into your path.

question: If you see a lane sign showing an arrow with the word ONLY beneath it above your lane, what does it mean?
options: a:You must proceed only in the direction shown by the arrow.,b:You should always change lanes immediately.,c:Follow the destination signs rather than the arrow.,d:The sign is advisory and can be ignored.
note: Lane control signs with arrows and ONLY require drivers in that lane to move in the indicated direction.

question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means what?
options: a:Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.,c:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits movement in the arrow's direction; drivers must stop and wait for a green signal to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:When traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the left.,b:When you increase your speed before the turn.,c:When traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the right.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street only when traffic on that street moves to the left and no sign prohibits the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what speed should you try to achieve?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.
note: When merging, match the speed of freeway traffic as closely as possible to merge smoothly and safely into traffic.

question: If you come to a railroad crossing with gates lowered and flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted.,b:Drive around the gates if no train is visible.,c:Slow down and proceed carefully past the gates.,d:Stop on the tracks to check both directions.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to go around lowered gates; wait until the gates are raised and lights stop flashing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,b:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,c:All of the above.
note: Always check mirrors and blind spots and signal to alert other drivers before changing lanes or passing.

question: If you park uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them to the right (toward the side of the road) so the vehicle would roll away from the center.,b:Leave them straight ahead.,c:Turn them left toward the center of the road.,d:Turn them toward the nearest driveway.
note: On hills without a curb, turn wheels so the vehicle would roll away from traffic (toward the side of the road) if brakes fail.

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:So others can see your vehicle.,b:To keep your engine warm.,c:To warn others of bad weather conditions.
note: Headlights make your vehicle more visible to other drivers in low visibility conditions. If you use windshield wipers, Alabama law also requires low beam headlights.

question: Why is it important to look far ahead while driving on a highway?
options: a:It reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Helps you keep up with traffic.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: Watching far ahead helps you anticipate stops and lane changes, reducing the need for sudden braking or swerving and improving fuel efficiency and traffic flow.

question: Accruing how many points on your license within two years will result in a one-year suspension?
options: a:24 or more,b:21 to 23,c:18 to 20
note: Under Alabama's point system, accumulating 24 or more points within a two-year period can result in a 365-day license suspension.

question: If you are about to be rear-ended, which action should you NOT take?
options: a:Press your head against the head restraint.,b:Brace yourself.,c:Release your seat belt.
note: Do not release your seat belt; brace and press against the head restraint to reduce injury from whiplash.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of what?
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,b:Being late for an appointment.,c:Missing an exit only.,d:Driving more carefully.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and slows reaction times, increasing the likelihood of falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or at an equipment check, what must a driver produce?
options: a:Only their license.,b:Only their insurance and registration.,c:Their license, insurance, and registration.
note: Drivers must present their driver's license, proof of vehicle registration, and proof of insurance when stopped for a violation or equipment check.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not enter an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red. When is it acceptable to enter in this situation?
options: a:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,b:Under any circumstances.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: Even if the signal is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even when no crosswalk is present; stop and allow them to finish crossing safely.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams while driving at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Flash your high beams to remind them to dim theirs.,d:Close your eyes briefly until the vehicle passes.
note: Avoid looking directly at blinding headlights; glance to the right edge of your lane and keep track of the approaching vehicle out of the corner of your eye.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Allow a larger following distance (3–4 seconds).,b:Be ready to use your horn often.,c:Drive more slowly than usual.,d:Follow at the same distance as you would a car.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and are more likely to fall; allow a longer following distance to give room to react.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you always do?
options: a:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear).,b:Turn your front wheels parallel to the road regardless of curb presence.,c:Leave the car in neutral if you expect to return soon.,d:One of your rear wheels must touch the curb.
note: Always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear); position wheels so a rolling vehicle moves away from traffic if brakes fail.

question: As you approach the crest of a hill, you should:
options: a:Speed up slightly to maintain momentum.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary and reduce speed as needed.,c:Maintain a steady speed regardless of visibility.,d:Move to the left side of the lane for a better view.
note: Because you cannot see what is beyond the top of a hill, slow and be prepared to stop if there is a hazard or stalled vehicle ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is an important step to take when making a turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions.,b:Always move to the left lane.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Before turning, check rear and side traffic to ensure the movement is safe and adjust speed appropriately.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Take a break.,b:Try to fight it.,c:Take some caffeine pills.
note: If you feel drowsy, stop at the nearest safe place to rest, nap, stretch, or switch drivers; caffeine is not a safe substitute for rest.

question: How must you yield right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive as closely to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,c:Stop immediately, even if you are within an intersection.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping; avoid stopping in intersections and only move when it is safe after they pass.

question: If you are involved in a minor collision with no injuries and little damage, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: If no one is injured and it is safe, move vehicles out of traffic to a safe location to reduce congestion and further risk.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what is still required for best protection?
options: a:Seat belts should still be worn.,b:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,c:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.
note: Airbags are supplemental; for maximum safety, always wear lap and shoulder belts together with airbags.

question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what is the correct braking action?
options: a:Apply the brakes lightly.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: If the vehicle is skidding, avoid braking; concentrate on steering to regain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No — do not drive on the shoulder to pass.,b:Only if the shoulder is wide enough.,c:If the vehicle ahead is turning left, pass on the shoulder.,d:If traffic is stopped, pass on the shoulder.
note: Passing on the shoulder is prohibited because other drivers do not expect vehicles there and may pull off the road.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to stay safe?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance and use headlights properly, switching to low beams for oncoming traffic.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop, yield to others, then go when the intersection is clear.

question: After passing a large truck, how should you re-enter the lane?
options: a:Give the truck plenty of room before you move back into the lane.,b:Re-enter immediately and then slow down.,c:Re-enter whenever you feel like it.,d:Cut in front quickly to prevent the truck from speeding up.
note: Do not return to your lane until you can see the truck's entire front in your rearview mirror; give large vehicles extra space for stopping.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.,b:Continue driving, but try to stay out of its way.,c:See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.
note: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop, allowing it to pass. Do not attempt to outrun it.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Maintaining a steady speed.,b:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling well in advance helps drivers behind you judge and keep a safe following distance.

question: Which habits are dangerous when driving through work zones?
options: a:Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers/equipment.,b:Only tailgating other vehicles.,c:Only failing to watch for workers and equipment.,d:Driving at posted speed limits.
note: In work zones you should reduce speed, avoid tailgating, and carefully watch for workers and equipment.

question: A broken yellow centerline between lanes indicates:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is never permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,d:Traffic flows in the same direction on both sides of the line.
note: A broken yellow centerline means you may cross to pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present; you may not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

question: At an intersection showing a flashing yellow light, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Stop, then enter the intersection when it is safe to do so.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light requires you to slow to a safe speed, look for hazards, and proceed with caution.

question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to do what?
options: a:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,b:Inconvenience drivers.,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
note: Work zone devices mark hazardous areas and direct traffic to protect both workers and road users; obey them and slow down.

question: Which action is appropriate when driving at night?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance in the dark to allow more time to respond; use high beams appropriately and avoid staring at oncoming lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on red after stopping?
options: a:You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,b:You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.,c:You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: After a full stop, turning left on red is only allowed from a one-way street onto another one-way street unless prohibited by signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed repeatedly on both sides while in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.,d:Increase speed to stay out of others' way.
note: On multi-lane roads, drive in the right lane unless passing or preparing for a left turn; use right lanes if traveling slower than traffic flow.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted and lights stop flashing.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are in sight.,c:Slowly pass the bus while watching for children.,d:Stop only if you are behind the bus.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing lights and extended stop arm until the bus moves and the signals are turned off.

question: Which statement about large trucks is correct?
options: a:They require longer distances to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They have air brakes that always allow rapid stops.,c:They are more maneuverable than cars.,d:They stop in the same distance as passenger cars.
note: Large trucks need substantially more distance to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed.

question: Which of the following is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,b:Using high beam headlights in fog.,c:Staring fixedly at the road ahead with no scanning.,d:Driving with only parking lights at night.
note: Regularly checking mirrors and scanning the road every 2–5 seconds helps you detect hazards; use low beams in fog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate from a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane on the interstate and speed up to match the flow of traffic.,b:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.
note: On a short ramp without an acceleration lane, wait for a safe gap in traffic and then accelerate to merge smoothly into traffic.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog, rain, or snow?
options: a:Low beams.,b:High beams.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow because high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: The measurement of alcohol in a person's blood is known as:
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,d:Breath alcohol index (BAI).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) expresses the percentage of alcohol in a person's bloodstream and indicates level of impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a Yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.,c:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: Slow or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to traffic close enough to be a hazard.

question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic light when you approach it?
options: a:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.,b:May not proceed until it changes to green.,c:You are traveling in the wrong direction.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop fully, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:No one.,b:Oncoming cars.,c:Overtaking cars.
note: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight; proceed only when it is safe and will not affect oncoming traffic.

question: Which statement about roadwork zones is true?
options: a:Fines are the same for violations committed in work zones as they are under normal traffic conditions.,b:You must 'Slow for the Cone Zone.'.,c:Slow down only if you think workers are present.
note: Drivers should slow for work zones and follow signage and instructions to protect workers and other road users.

question: What is the only factor that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat,b:Drinking caffeine,c:Time
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol from the bloodstream.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn.,b:Quickly turn in front of the truck to avoid delay.,c:Squeeze between the vehicle and the curb to turn.,d:Sound your horn and pass on the right.
note: Do not try to fit between a turning large vehicle and the curb; wait until it finishes its turn to avoid a collision.

question: In bad weather, what steering and braking technique should you use?
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly.,b:Steer off the road.,c:Drive in a low gear.
note: Smooth steering and braking help maintain vehicle control in inclement weather; avoid sudden inputs that could cause skids.

question: Excessive speed often results in:
options: a:High-risk decision-making.,b:Increased ability to react to a hazard.,c:No change in crash risk.
note: Excessive speed is a leading factor in crashes and increases the severity of collisions and likelihood of poor choices.

question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line, what is permitted?
options: a:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.,b:You cannot cross the line to pass.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and indicate lane changes and passing are allowed when safe.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what does that mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is permitted from the right.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate lanes of opposite directions and prohibit passing from either direction.

question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic mean?
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Dashed yellow center lines separate two-way traffic and permit passing when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should be your first response?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: If a vehicle merges too closely ahead, lift your foot off the accelerator to create space without slamming on the brakes or swerving dangerously.

question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line indicate for the side with the broken line?
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe.,b:Vehicles on both sides may pass anytime.,c:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.,d:No passing allowed for either side.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe; a solid line means no passing from that side.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Speed up.
note: Tire traction is reduced on wet, snowy, or icy roads; slow down and adjust driving to conditions to maintain control.

question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?
options: a:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,b:Stop, proceeding only when all the pedestrians have crossed.,c:Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: Do not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk; pedestrians may be crossing and obscured from your view. Stop and wait until the crossing is clear.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Warning.,b:Yield.,c:Stop.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of special conditions or hazards ahead, and are usually yellow or orange.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you must stop on snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With Anti-Lock Braking Systems, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will modulate braking to prevent wheel lockup.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as what?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows nerve impulses and bodily functions, impairing judgment, coordination, and alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a turn lane to prepare for a left turn where there is oncoming traffic, what should you do before turning?
options: a:Signal well in advance and keep your front wheels pointed straight until you begin the turn.,b:Turn your front wheels left to be ready to turn.,c:Move to the left of the center lane and stop.,d:Honk to warn oncoming traffic.
note: Signal about 100 feet before turning and keep wheels straight to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.

question: Your vehicle may hydroplane at speeds as low as approximately:
options: a:35 miles per hour.,b:40 miles per hour.,c:45 miles per hour.,d:25 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds around 35 mph when standing water prevents tires from channeling water away.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always drive at what speed?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,b:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,c:At the speed limit.
note: Drive at a speed that is safe for current road, traffic, and weather conditions; never exceed posted limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

question: When should you allow an extra cushion of space around your vehicle?
options: a:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,b:When following a small passenger car.,c:When following a station wagon.
note: Increase following distance behind trucks, buses, and vehicles towing trailers because they have large blind spots and may block your view of the road.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, what should you try to do?
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Stop in the right lane.,c:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
note: If possible, move the vehicle completely off the traveled portion of the road to avoid creating a hazard.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal mean for turning in that direction?
options: a:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,b:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow means stop; drivers must remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears and must not turn against the red arrow.

question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to drive through it.,c:Shift into neutral as you go through the water.,d:Brake hard before entering the puddle.
note: Avoid large standing water when possible to prevent hydroplaning or vehicle damage; choose a safer path.

question: When near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid?
options: a:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,b:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large commercial vehicles have extensive blind spots on each side; avoid lingering beside them so the truck driver can see you and you can see the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, how should your speed compare to freeway traffic?
options: a:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,b:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,c:At the legal speed limit.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of highway traffic so you can merge smoothly.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: Ease off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning until the tires regain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If many vehicles are passing you on the right while you are driving in the left lane and the driver behind you wants to go faster, what should you do?
options: a:Move into the right lane when it is safe.,b:Stay in your lane so you don't impede the flow of traffic.,c:Drive onto the left shoulder to let the other vehicles pass.
note: When driving slower than others in the left lane, move into the right lane when safe to allow faster vehicles to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should enter:
options: a:Any available lane.,b:The second lane from the curb.,c:The first (closest) lane on the one-way street.,d:The farthest lane from the curb.
note: When turning from a two-way onto a one-way street, turn into the nearest (first) legal lane of the one-way street.

question: Regulatory signs generally are which of the following?
options: a:White,b:Green,c:Yellow
note: Regulatory signs inform drivers of laws and rules that must be followed; they are most commonly white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green symbols or letters.

question: Before backing a vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Both walk around the vehicle and look to the front, sides, and rear.,b:Walk completely around the vehicle to be sure no person or obstacle is behind it.,c:Look to the front, sides, and rear.
note: When preparing to back up, walk around the vehicle if possible to check for obstacles or people, then look front, sides, and rear and continue to look over your shoulder while backing. Do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins skidding to the left, what should you do?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,b:Not turn your steering wheel.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: If your vehicle skids, take your foot off the accelerator, avoid braking, and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control. (If equipped with ABS, brake firmly and steer straight.)

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Using your side mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using the inside rearview mirror.
note: Turn your head toward the lane you intend to enter to see areas not visible in mirrors before changing lanes.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is in poor condition, what can it cause?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: A failing suspension can make the vehicle hard to control and affect ride comfort and handling; have it inspected and repaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter a roadway, what should you do regarding the sidewalk?
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.,c:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
note: You must stop before entering the sidewalk area; pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

question: Why should high beam headlights not be used in fog or mist?
options: a:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,b:The light will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.,c:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,d:High beams are illegal in foggy conditions.
note: High beams reflect off fog or mist back toward the driver, worsening visibility; use low beams instead.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:Traffic light ahead.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line on your side indicates that passing is prohibited.

question: When driving in work zones, what is a safe practice?
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: Increase following distance in work zones and avoid tailgating to allow time to react to sudden stops or lane shifts.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway compared to a city street?
options: a:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:In order to see potential hazards early.
note: On freeways, watching farther ahead gives you more time to react to rapid changes, merges, and hazards.

question: Motorcycles on the road are entitled to what lane width?
options: a:The width of the sidewalk.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:One-half of the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full lane width, and other drivers should avoid sharing a lane with them and watch for their presence.

question: How can you check vehicles that are in your blind spots?
options: a:Look over your shoulders.,b:Only use the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only use the outside rearview mirrors.,d:Trust the sensors to detect them.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen with mirrors alone; glance over your shoulder to check these areas before changing lanes.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow when visibility is poor, you should:
options: a:Turn on your parking lights.,b:Increase instrument panel lighting only.,c:Turn on your headlights (low beams).,d:Use high beam headlights for better visibility.
note: Use your headlights when visibility is reduced; low beams are appropriate during rain, snow, fog, or when windshield wipers are in use.

question: Which statement best describes backing your vehicle?
options: a:Backing up is always hazardous and requires extra caution.,b:Backing up is only dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Backing up is only dangerous in large vehicles.,d:Backing is safer than driving forward.
note: Backing is risky because it's hard to see behind the vehicle; use care and aids like a spotter when possible.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection allows you to do what?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:Continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed, if it is clear to do so.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection, yielding to traffic or pedestrians already in it and proceeding when safe.

question: If dust or smoke reduce visibility, what lights should you use?
options: a:Headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers only.,d:Hazard lights without headlights.
note: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles and when others may have difficulty seeing you.

question: While in a vehicle on a highway, is it legal to have or drink from an open container of alcohol?
options: a:It is illegal to either drink from or possess open containers of alcohol.,b:It is legal to drink alcohol if you're not driving.,c:It is legal to drink alcohol if you're driving but not drunk.
note: It is illegal in Alabama to possess or consume open alcoholic beverage containers in a motor vehicle on a highway while it is being operated.

question: If you see a pedestrian crossing your lane where there is no marked crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.,b:Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.,c:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,d:Honk to urge them to hurry.
note: Even without a marked crosswalk, you must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane and allow them to finish crossing.

question: What does a pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Stop sign.,b:Regulatory sign.,c:School zone or school crossing sign.
note: A five-sided (pentagon) sign is used to warn drivers of school zones or school crossings where children may be present.

question: When using windshield wipers in rain, snow, or sleet, what else must you do?
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Honk intermittently to alert other drivers to the lowered visibility.
note: Alabama law requires drivers to turn on low beam headlights whenever windshield wipers are in use because of weather conditions.

question: How should you behave when you approach a person crossing the street using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the person is safely clear of your path.,b:Honk to let them know you're there and proceed slowly.,c:Carefully drive around them without stopping.,d:Wave them on to cross quickly.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way; stop until they are well away from your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers are required to obey instructions from which of the following persons at construction sites?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Drivers must obey flaggers and any temporary traffic control instructions in construction zones to ensure safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Slow down but never stop.
note: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic close enough to create a hazard; be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window and keep driving.,c:Drink a caffeinated beverage and continue driving.,d:Turn off the radio to concentrate.
note: To avoid the hazards of fatigue, stop and rest or swap drivers; short naps are effective at restoring alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you tell you have enough space to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,b:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,c:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: You should only move back into the lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning in rain, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Put on cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: Lower your speed in rainy weather to reduce the risk of hydroplaning; driving too fast can cause tires to lose contact with the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection means you must:
options: a:Treat it the same as a stop sign (stop, yield, then go).,b:Expect the light to turn green shortly.,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,d:Treat it only as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when the way is clear—same as a stop sign.

question: Why is night driving more challenging?
options: a:The speed limit is increased at night.,b:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.,c:Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes judging distance and the speed of other vehicles more difficult; drive within the range of your headlights.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Construction and maintenance warnings.,b:General warning signs.,c:Regulatory instructions like speed limits.,d:Guide signs for motorists.
note: Orange signs are used specifically to indicate construction and maintenance warnings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you frequently pass other cars on a two-lane road by speeding, what is the likely result?
options: a:You will increase your chances of a collision.,b:You will arrive more quickly and more safely.,c:You will help reduce traffic congestion.,d:You will minimize your risk of an accident.
note: Repeated passing on two-lane roads increases exposure to oncoming traffic and raising the chance of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.,c:You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
note: Yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection; yield when turning on a steady green.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b:The truck driver to stop the vehicle.,c:Other drivers when they want to slow down.
note: Large trucks require more distance to stop than cars; leaving extra space in front of a truck allows the truck driver room to brake safely.

question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on a layer of water. How can you help prevent it?
options: a:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning is more likely at higher speeds on wet pavement; slow down to reduce the risk of losing contact with the road.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:Loading zone.,b:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.
note: A red curb means stopping, standing, or parking is not allowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no-passing zone, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
note: Slow down or move right when safe to allow the passing vehicle to return to its lane as soon as possible.

question: When a school bus is stopped to pick up or drop off children, what must motorists do?
options: a:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Stop if you are driving in the same direction.
note: Drivers must stop in all directions when a school bus has its stop arm out and red lights flashing, so children can board or disembark safely.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Left, toward the center of the road,b:Straight ahead,c:Right, toward the side of the road
note: When parking downhill without a curb, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If stopped at a red light but a green arrow points your direction, when may you proceed?
options: a:Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:First come to a complete stop.,c:Wait until the light changes.
note: A green arrow gives protected movement in its direction if you are in the proper lane; still yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.,b:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,c:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop.
note: Slow down, obey posted limits, and be ready for sudden stops or workers and equipment near the roadway.

question: What message is displayed on a red octagon-shaped sign?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:One-way.,c:Stop.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) red sign always means 'STOP' and requires a full stop at the sign.

question: To minimize glare from the headlights of an oncoming car, what should you do?
options: a:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Keep your focus on the centerline of the road.,c:Flash your high beams back to the other driver.,d:Close one eye until the car passes.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights; glance briefly to the right edge of your lane and monitor the vehicle peripherally.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,b:Just after it starts to rain.,c:When they are clean and dry.
note: Roads are often most slippery shortly after rain begins because water mixes with oil and other residues on the surface.

question: Do sudden wind gusts on highways affect only large vehicles?
options: a:No — they can affect all vehicles and cause problems.,b:Yes — only large vehicles are affected.,c:They only cause visibility issues, not handling problems.,d:They only affect motorcycles.
note: Strong wind can reduce visibility and affect the handling of all vehicles, though large vehicles may be especially impacted.

question: Continuous hard braking on ice or snow often causes what problem?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: Hard continuous braking on icy surfaces can lock the wheels and cause loss of steering; slow gradually and use controlled braking.

question: When must a vehicle be covered by liability insurance?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only when used on an interstate.,c:Only when operated by a minor.
note: Alabama law requires motor vehicles used on public roads to be covered by liability insurance to protect consumers involved in accidents.

question: When driving in fog, you should use which type of headlights?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Because larger vehicles need longer distances to stop and may not be able to avoid a collision.,b:Because small vehicles cannot see large vehicles in their rearview mirrors.,c:Because large vehicles always travel faster than small ones.,d:Because large vehicles have priority on the road.
note: Large trucks and buses, due to their weight and size, require longer stopping distances; sudden stops in front of them are dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?
options: a:Change lanes abruptly or without signaling.,b:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Check mirrors for approaching vehicles.,d:Ensure the lane is clear before moving over.
note: Never change lanes suddenly; always signal, check mirrors, and verify blind spots to ensure safety.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle when which condition is met?
options: a:Vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.,b:The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:The yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.
note: A broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line indicates that traffic on the side with the broken line may pass when safe; crossing double solid lines is not allowed.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,b:Continue ahead because the motorist has the right-of-way.,c:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until they have finished crossing before proceeding.
